rows.context: The 1979 revival diagnosis and the earlier 1978 Tuchman review are distinct interventions. In the review he praises communication while questioning the selection of events and explanatory depth. The 1979 essay restricts its diagnosis to a prominent minority and acknowledges continuing quantitative work.

existing_sources_reused.title: Linda A. Pollock, The Forgotten Children (PhD thesis, University of St Andrews, 1981).
existing_sources_reused.citation: Linda A. Pollock, The Forgotten Children (PhD thesis, University of St Andrews, 1981).

verification.note: Repository abstract and downloaded primary thesis read at pp. 31, 96–98 and 143–144. Supports explicit separation of Ariès’s childhood concept from affection, criticism of sweeping change/Stone’s explanatory wording and selective use of diaries, plus attention to literate diarists, censorship and generalization. Thesis and 1983 book are distinct records; no assumption of identical text. OCR dates in the repository abstract are unreliable and not repeated. Additional 2026-09-12 reading: complete section 2.2.3, printed pp. 93–94, criticizes deMause’s source selection and progressive narrative. Laslett/Shore quotations remain mediated; their predictions are not adopted. This is the 1981 thesis, not the independently unread 1983 book criticized by deMause in 1988.

verification.note: Title, author and 1977 metadata checked; listing mixes edition information and is not used to settle publisher/abridgment details. Pollock’s separately read primary thesis pp. 96–98 supplies evidence of criticism of Stone’s affective-individualism explanation and use of personal documents.

verification.note: Primary title/imprint and printed 21–29 read through local OCR; imprint visually checked. First Harper paperback 1979, copyright 1977/1979; distinct from the existing 1977 record. Pages 22–24 qualify change by reversals, social strata and overlapping family types; 25 assumes surviving personal documents broadly representative despite intimate material destroyed; 26–27 acknowledge literate-minority bias and difficulties selecting representative cases. Remaining scan and original records unread; the author’s representativeness assumption is not independently validated.

verification.note: Primary PDF read: printed 3–6 and 13–24 complete; 7–12 unread. Page 3 visually inspected, 5 and 13–23 OCR recovered because embedded text clips lines; 4, 6 and 24 read embedded text. Includes all notes on these pages, not all article notes. Starn directs Stone to White; examples and methodological limits are explicit. Broad historiographical diagnoses, dismissive descriptions and implied psychologies remain Stone’s claims. Montaillou citation 1976 is not adopted as first publication; quoted Elias reception/edition shorthand not certified. Prior Oxford metadata retained; book bodies not thereby read.
